notes:
Context: Lakemere builds a marketplace analytics product used by two-sided marketplaces (buyers + sellers). They plan to ship a contextual chat assistant (support) and an embeddings-powered marketplace search + rerank for buyer intent. Started on Hosted API, but due to predictable traffic patterns and requirement for VPC network isolation they want Dedicated.

POC / Technical summary:
- Hosted API trial showed token latency 60-80ms median for short chitchat; acceptable.
- Production needs: low tail latency (p95 < 200ms), steady throughput for peak hours (~120 reqs/s across services), embeddings job batch (~10k vectors/day).
- Preferred models: open Llama-family / LRC-optimized weights; indifferent to exact checkpoint if Redwood can guarantee latency/cost profile.
- Routing/fallback: prefer smart routing to cheaper variant on non-critical routes; need canary rollout.

Pricing/packaging discussion (primary topic):
- They asked for committed capacity pricing for Dedicated: starting target ~200k tokens/day equivalent, with 2x burst allowance during campaigns.
- Want overage defined as simple per-token rate (no complex credits). Proposed Redwood tiers: 3 commitment bands (starter, growth, enterprise) with progressive discounts and optional burst pool.
- Ramp schedule: 3-month ramp from starter -> growth with defined check-ins and metric gates (latency, cost per token).
- Key ask from procurement: a one-line SLI + credit terms for missed SLA, and predictable monthly invoice modeling for finance.
- Legal/security: need SOC2 report (in last 12 months), SSO/SAML setup, audit log export, and KMS integration notes. Data residency: US only for now.

Call quotes / seller notes:
- "We like the predictability of Dedicated and want a pricing model that's easy to forecast month-to-month." — Head of Product, Lakemere.
- AE notes: leaning toward 12-month commitment but want 3-month measurable ramp to reduce risk.

Open items / negotiation points:
- Exact committed tokens/day and discount level. Finance prefers $/token over complex seat models.
- Burst policy: whether burst is free up to 2x for short windows or charged at a blended overage rate.
- SLA credit language and cadence for remediation.
- Onboarding fee vs included dev-hours for tuning batching/quantization.

Stubs / links: pricing deck + POC config in Drive (see linked_drive_docs). Fireflies IDs above for call transcripts. Jira ticket INF-9134 opened for security proof request.

Recommended Redwood playbook: offer a 12-month contract with a 3-month ramp, starter committed band at medium discount, explicit burst pool (2x for 72 hours/month) and a straightforward overage per-token price. Include 10 dev-hours of onboarding and SOC2 evidence + KMS integration notes in the SOW to unblock procurement quickly.

Short-term next steps (as of 2025-03-07):
- Draft SOW with three commitment bands and a sample invoice model (Maya).
- Legal to send SOC2 package and KMS integration docs (security team).
- Schedule procurement + finance call to sign off on ARR model (week of 2025-03-10).
- Technical POC env for Dedicated ready within 5 business days after SOW sign.
notes_short: Mid-market marketplace SaaS evaluating Hosted -> Dedicated. Focused on committed tokens, burst policy, simple overage pricing, SOC2 + KMS. Legal & procurement are blockers; agreed 3-month ramp and require SOW with invoice modeling.
additional_comments: Finance asked for an amortized monthly view of committed spend vs expected usage; proposed sample workbook in Drive.
